'''Flávio da Conceição''' (born 12 June 1974) is a Brazilian former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[defensive midfielder]].

Conceição enjoyed a successful career in Spain, where he played for two clubs—including [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] with whom he won six major titles—and also represented [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] on more than 40 occasions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Appearances for Brazil National Team|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/braz-recintlp.html|access-date=29 March 2017|website=[[RSSSF]]}}</ref>

==Club career==
Born in [[Santa Maria da Serra]], [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]], Conceição began his career with [[Rio Branco Esporte Clube|Rio Branco]] in 1992. He then joined [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] a year later, and racked up over 100 first-team appearances during his spell. This caught the attention of Spanish club [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]], who paid [[Euro|€]]5.2&nbsp;million for him after the [[1996 Summer Olympics]].

Playing alongside compatriot [[Mauro Silva]] in central midfield, Conceição gradually developed into a key force in the [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicians]]' rise in [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/these-football-times/2016/feb/12/la-liga-unpedictable-league-deportivo-barcelona-real-madrid|title=When La Liga was just as unpredictable as this season's Premier League|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=12 February 2016|access-date=29 March 2017}}</ref> as he scored four goals in 27 games in the team's [[1999–2000 La Liga|1999–2000 league conquest]]. This led to a 2000 move to fellow [[La Liga]] side [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]], worth €26&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://elpais.com/diario/2000/08/01/deportes/965080802_850215.html|title=El Madrid intenta tapar con el fichaje de Flavio Conceiçao la marcha de Redondo|trans-title=Madrid try to compensate Redondo departure with signing of Flavio Conceiçao|newspaper=[[El País]]|language=es|date=1 August 2000|access-date=29 March 2017|last1=Sanz|first1=Óscar}}</ref>

Although he appeared sparingly, Conceição did win two league titles and the [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League|2001–02 edition]] of the [[UEFA Champions League]] – in that competition, he set up [[Steve McManaman]] for the closing 2–0 semi-final win against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] at the [[Camp Nou]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2001/matches/round=1548/match=1024727/postmatch/report/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130926001212/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2001/matches/round=1548/match=1024727/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 September 2013|title=Madrid magic beats Barcelona|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=24 April 2002|access-date=29 March 2017}}</ref> He spent the [[2003–04 Bundesliga|2003–04 campaign]] on loan to [[Borussia Dortmund]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.welt.de/print-welt/article250716/Nur-Flavio-Conceicao-macht-Borussia-Dortmund-Mut.html|title=Nur Flavio Conceicao macht Borussia Dortmund Mut|trans-title=Only Flavio Conceicao emboldens Borussia Dortmund|newspaper=[[Die Welt]]|language=de|date=4 August 2003|access-date=29 March 2017|last1=Müller|first1=Oliver}}</ref> where he was also irregularly played.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.faz.net/aktuell/sport/fussball/borussia-dortmund-leihen-und-sparen-1148616.html|title=Leihen und sparen|trans-title=Loaning and saving|newspaper=[[Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung]]|language=de|date=29 January 2004|access-date=29 March 2017}}</ref>

In the summer of 2004, Conceição moved to Turkey's [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]]. In [[2004–05 Süper Lig|his first and only season]], he won the [[Turkish Cup]] but failed to make the Champions League, thus activating a clause in his contract which allowed him to leave, and he signed for [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]] of Greece.

Afflicted with injuries and loss of form, Conceição was released and retired at the age of 32.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/sp/campinas-e-regiao/noticia/2013/01/lembra-dele-corte-na-copa-de-98-ainda-incomoda-flavio-conceicao.html|title=Lembra dele? Corte na Copa de 98 ainda incomoda Flávio Conceição|trans-title=Remember him? 98 Cup cut still bothers Flávio Conceição|publisher=[[Rede Globo|Globo Esporte]]|language=pt|date=15 January 2013|access-date=29 March 2017}}</ref>

==International career==
Conceição earned 45 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] and scored four goals, and was part of the nation's [[1997 Copa América|1997]] and [[1999 Copa América|1999]] [[Copa América]]-winning sides.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tables/97safull.html|title=Copa América 1997|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=29 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tables/99safull.html|title=Copa América 1999|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=29 March 2017}}</ref> He was also picked for two [[FIFA Confederations Cup]] tournaments, making four appearances in the [[1997 FIFA Confederations Cup|1997 edition]] for the eventual champions.<ref name=FIFA>{{FIFA player|162612}}</ref>

In addition, Conceição [[Football at the 1996 Summer Olympics|won a bronze medal]] at the 1996 Olympics in [[Atlanta]],<ref name=FIFA/> but was never summoned for any [[FIFA World Cup]].
